inputs.text: The Liberal Party is fracturing from within, with some MPs agitating for a leadership rethink, but the real danger comes from those trying to pull it toward higher taxes on gas companies and scrapping concessions that protect property investors and preserve family wealth built on hard work. Angus Taylor has rightly rejected Andrew Hastie’s call for the party to be “open-minded” about these shifts, standing firm for the economic strength that comes from personal responsibility instead of progressive schemes that punish achievement. The opposition leader showed proper judgment by refusing to back Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump, resisting the usual left-wing attacks on a leader who puts national interests first. At the same time, the failure to clearly support the US and Israel’s war with Iran only weakens the authority we need to confront genuine threats and uphold social order.
